title: Methacholine challenge test
what: You breathe in a substance in small, slowly rising doses and do a breathing test, called spirometry, after each one. This checks how sensitive your airways are.
why: When asthma is suspected but a regular spirometry is normal.
duration: usually 1 to 2 hours; the result is given right away
tell_doctor: All inhalers and medicines. Some must be stopped ahead of time, but only as your doctor says
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding
If you had a heart attack, a stroke, or a recent cold
If you have high blood pressure

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Many inhalers and allergy pills are stopped for different lengths of time before the test. Your doctor will give you the plan. Do not stop anything on your own.

prepare.title: Coffee
prepare.text: On the day of the test, you usually cannot have coffee, tea, cola, or chocolate. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Smoking and exercise
prepare.text: Do not smoke or exercise on the day of the test.

prepare.title: Your health
prepare.text: If you catch a cold, call the clinic. The test is usually moved.

steps: First, you do a regular spirometry test
You breathe in a small dose of the substance through a nebulizer
After a couple of minutes, you do spirometry again
The dose is slowly increased and the steps repeated
The test stops when your readings drop or the full program is done
At the end, you get an inhaler to bring your breathing back to normal
feel: You may cough or feel slight tightness in your chest
Sometimes wheezing. The doctor is right there and will relieve it with an inhaler
Blowing out so many times can be tiring
after: You can leave when your breathing is back to where it started
You are usually told the result right away
You can go back to your medicines. Ask your doctor
red_flags: Cough or shortness of breath comes back at home and the inhaler does not help: call emergency services
Wheezing in the chest and trouble speaking

faq.a: The test is done under a doctor's watch, with medicines ready. Strong reactions are rare.
Otherwise the test may give a wrong result. Only your doctor decides what to stop and for how long.

reminders.text: Methacholine test tomorrow. Check which medicines your doctor told you not to take. No coffee or tea in the morning. Bring your inhaler.
